title: Stop a slow card check from holding up the terminal's connection

blocks.text: A merchant group says its busiest tills time out on purchases several times an hour, while quieter tills on the same server never do. The server answers purchases in `CardCheckListener`, which looks every card up in the blocked-card table. Under load a lookup takes a few seconds.

The table can't be made faster this quarter. Change `CardCheckListener` in `src/main/java/com/example/practice/CardCheckListener.java` so that a slow lookup no longer keeps a terminal waiting longer than its own purchase takes. The answer each terminal gets stays exactly what it is today, and `answer(...)` already builds and sends it.
Finish the two places marked `TODO`, in `process` and `newWorkers`. About five lines in total.
The tests call `process` the way a QServer session would and use a card table whose lookups they can hold and release. One test keeps two lookups running at once on one connection.

cases.says: every purchase is answered on its connection, 00 for a good card and 62 for a blocked one
process returns while the lookup is still running, so the session can read the connection's next message
a purchase whose lookup is quick is answered while an earlier, slow lookup is still running

origin.section: 3.3 A Listener Holds Up Its Own Connection

concepts: A listener runs on its connection's only reader thread, so slow work in it delays every later message on that connection but not other connections; slow work is handed off.
